title: Onboard real second outfit for Jason Cross and verify variant toggling end-to-end
description: End-to-end verification for Phase 2 (depends on scarecrow-zlp: author_outfit_variant.py implementation). Use author_outfit_variant.py to onboard one real additional outfit (or hair) DBZ artifact onto the existing artifacts/JasonCross_imported.blend master, then register it in scarecrow_pipeline/registry.py's CharacterRecord.outfits (or .hair) list for jason_cross so sprite_set.py's combo validation picks it up.
acceptance_criteria: Headless render with the new outfit active shows only its meshes visible (old outfit hidden); headless render with the original base outfit active still matches the pre-change reference render (regression check, e.g. via Pillow pixel/alpha diff); registry.json reflects the new outfit name; a sprite_set.py combo referencing the new outfit name resolves and validates without error.
close_reason: Onboarded Worker Uniform (Genesis 9 Daz Original) as second outfit for Jason Cross via author_outfit_variant.py. Fixed two bugs found during verification: (1) variant collection was linked to scene root instead of nested under the character collection, so worker.py's append_collection() would never pull it in; (2) a ReferenceError crash on the post-cleanup diagnostic print (accessed .name on already-deleted objects). Verified end-to-end: outfit toggle renders show only the active outfit's meshes; base-outfit regression render vs pre-change reference differs only by Cycles sampling noise (0.05% of pixels, alpha unchanged); registry.json updated with Outfit_WorkerUniform; sprite_set.py combo resolution validates the new outfit name and correctly rejects unregistered ones.

title: Implement blender/author_outfit_variant.py
description: Closes the gap where set_variant_visibility (worker.py:32) can only toggle Outfit_<name>/Hair_<name> collections that already exist in a master blend -- nothing today creates them. Add blender/author_outfit_variant.py, invoked headlessly like import_daz_artifact.py (blender -b <master.blend> -P author_outfit_variant.py -- --dbz <outfit.dbz> --collection-name <name> --kind outfit|hair [--out <versioned.blend>]): given the existing master .blend (already open) and a second DAZ outfit/hair DBZ artifact exported the same way as the base character (import_daz_artifact.py's easy_import_daz pattern), imports it into the open scene, fits/parents the new mesh(es) to the existing armature (useMakePosable/fitMeshes=DBZFILE against the already-present rig, not a fresh one), renames the resulting collection to the Outfit_<name>/Hair_<name> convention set_variant_visibility (blender/worker.py:32,200) expects, and re-saves the master blend (in place or to a new versioned copy via --out).
acceptance_criteria: Running the script against the Jason Cross master blend with a real outfit DBZ produces a collection named Outfit_<name> (or Hair_<name>) containing the new meshes correctly parented to the existing armature; set_variant_visibility can toggle it; the base character/outfit collections and existing render output are unaffected (no duplicate armature, no orphaned objects).
close_reason: Implemented blender/author_outfit_variant.py: imports a second DBZ into the open master blend, merges its rig into the existing armature via daz.merge_rigs(ALL_RIGS), de-dupes re-imported content via Blender's .NNN collision suffix, and collects the remainder into an Outfit_<name>/Hair_<name> collection. End-to-end verification against a real DBZ is scarecrow-2oz.

title: Implement scripts/generate_sprite_set.py CLI orchestrator
description:
Add scripts/generate_sprite_set.py, a CLI that takes a SpriteSetSpec JSON file (from scarecrow_pipeline/sprite_set.py, T1/scarecrow-scarecrow-uc0.1) and renders every combo.

For each (filename, RenderRequest) from SpriteSetSpec.expand():
1. Write the RenderRequest to a temp/scratch JSON file (e.g. under the spec's output_dir, or Python tempfile -- avoid clobbering between combos)
2. Invoke blender headless once per combo via subprocess: blender --background <scene-or-master-blend> --python blender/worker.py -- --request <request.json>. Follow the exact invocation pattern already used throughout this session (see e.g. how blender/worker.py's own CLI is documented in its module docstring, and how prior validation scripts in this session invoked blender via subprocess with '--' argument separation and ABSOLUTE paths -- a past bug this session found: relative --out-dir/output paths passed to a Blender subprocess can resolve against the wrong drive/cwd in headless mode on Windows; always pass absolute paths).
3. Do NOT try to batch multiple renders inside one Blender process -- worker.py:render() mutates shared scene/compositor/shadow-catcher state in ways not proven safe to call repeatedly in one process. One subprocess per render for this phase.
4. Collect a manifest: list of {combo fields, output_path, status: 'ok'|'failed', stderr on failure} and write it as JSON (e.g. <output_dir>/manifest.json) alongside the rendered PNGs.
5. Surface non-zero subprocess exit codes / stderr clearly per combo rather than failing the whole batch silently or halting on first failure -- continue through the batch and report failures in the manifest.

CLI args: at minimum --spec <spec.json> --blender-exe <path to blender.exe, or read from config/toolchain.json> --master-blend <override, optional>.

Context: this is Phase 1 of C:\Users\ghirp\.claude\plans\now-let-s-plan-for-atomic-wadler.md. Read that file and the T1 task (scarecrow-scarecrow-uc0.1) for full background.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/generate_sprite_set.py exists and is runnable as a CLI
- Given a SpriteSetSpec JSON with N combos, produces N PNG files (or fewer + failure entries in the manifest, never silently fewer with no explanation)
- Writes a manifest.json mapping each combo to its output path and status
- Uses absolute paths for all Blender subprocess file arguments
- One Blender subprocess per combo, not a shared long-lived process
close_reason: Added scripts/generate_sprite_set.py CLI orchestrator: one subprocess per combo, absolute paths, manifest.json with ok/failed status, continues past failures. 3 new pytest cases, all 10 tests pass.

title: Verify sprite-set generation end-to-end against Jason Cross
description:
Headless end-to-end verification of scripts/generate_sprite_set.py (T2/scarecrow-scarecrow-uc0.2) using the real onboarded character.

Use artifacts/registry.json's JasonCross record (master_blend=artifacts/JasonCross_imported.blend, collection=Jasoncross_v1) as the character/master_blend source. Since Phase 2 (outfit authoring) may not have landed yet, only one outfit exists -- so build the verification spec with combos varying ONLY emotion (e.g. 3 FACSExpression variants using controls confirmed valid in docs/facs_controls.json, such as facs_bs_JawOpenWide) and optionally pose (using bone names confirmed valid in docs/posable_bones.json, e.g. r_upperarm/spine1 as used in this session's own validation renders). If an outfit variant DOES exist by the time this task is picked up, extend the verification spec to include it too.

Steps:
1. Construct a SpriteSetSpec JSON with e.g. 3 emotion combos (neutral + 2 expressions).
2. Run scripts/generate_sprite_set.py against it, headless.
3. Assert: output PNG count matches combo count (or manifest correctly reports any failures), each PNG has an alpha channel (open via PIL and check mode/getchannel('A') has non-trivial variance, i.e. it's not all-opaque or all-transparent), filenames match the manifest.
4. Spot-check at least one non-neutral-expression PNG visually differs from the neutral one (can reuse the pixel-diff or visual-read approach used earlier this session for FACS validation).

Clean up any large generated PNGs/blends from artifacts/ after verification the same way this session cleaned up prior diagnostic artifacts (don't leave multi-hundred-MB throwaway renders committed).

Context: this is Phase 1 of C:\Users\ghirp\.claude\plans\now-let-s-plan-for-atomic-wadler.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- A real headless run of scripts/generate_sprite_set.py against artifacts/JasonCross_imported.blend succeeds
- manifest.json correctly reflects what was rendered
- At least one non-neutral render is visually confirmed to differ from the neutral baseline
- No large throwaway artifacts left committed after verification
notes: Real headless verification against Jason Cross uncovered and fixed 4 real bugs that blocked scarecrow-uc0.2's implementation from ever actually rendering (previously masked because: 1) tests/test_generate_sprite_set.py only exercises a mocked subprocess.run, never real Blender; 2) Blender exits 0 on an unhandled Python exception in background mode unless --python-exit-code is passed, so the manifest was falsely reporting every combo as ok). Fixes: (a) scripts/generate_sprite_set.py opened master_blend itself as the --background scene, but worker.py then tries to append the character collection FROM that same file -- 'Cannot load from the current blend file'; now launches against Blender's blank default scene and passes --python-exit-code 1. (b) scarecrow_pipeline/sprite_set.py passed SpriteSetSpec.character (display name, e.g. 'JasonCross') as RenderRequest.character, but worker.py's append_collection() needs the actual master_blend collection name (registry says 'Jasoncross_v1') -- now resolves via CharacterRecord.collection. (c)-(e) blender/compositor.py used Blender <4.x compositor APIs no longer valid in 5.1: Scene.node_tree removed (now Scene.compositing_node_group + bpy.data.node_groups.new), CompositorNodeComposite node type no longer exists inside a node group, CompositorNodeAlphaOver socket order changed (was Fac/Image1/Image2, now Background/Foreground/Factor/Type/StraightAlpha), CompositorNodeOutputFile lost file_slots/base_path (now file_name/directory) and defaults format.media_type to MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE which blocks PNG until set to IMAGE. After all fixes: 3/3 real headless renders succeeded, manifest matched, alpha channel had real variance (std~90) on all 3 PNGs, and the jaw-open render was visually confirmed (both pixel-diff and visual read) to differ from neutral. Cleaned up the 127MB verification output dir after confirming.
close_reason: Real headless verification succeeded (3/3 renders, manifest correct, alpha channel + visual diff confirmed) after fixing 4 real bugs uncovered in the process: master_blend/scene collision in generate_sprite_set.py, wrong collection name in sprite_set.py, and 3 Blender 5.1 compositor API breaks in compositor.py. See issue notes for details.

title: Implement SpriteSetSpec model + RenderRequest expansion
description:
Add scarecrow_pipeline/sprite_set.py. Reuse RenderRequest/PosePayload/FACSExpression from scarecrow_pipeline/schemas.py UNCHANGED -- do not modify them.

Define a Pydantic SpriteSetSpec model:
- character: str, master_blend: str (or resolve both via scarecrow_pipeline.registry.Registry.load() by character name -- prefer looking up the registry entry over requiring both explicitly, since artifacts/registry.json already has a seeded JasonCross record with collection='Jasoncross_v1')
- base_camera: CameraMetadata (default), base_lighting: SceneLighting (default)
- combos: list of {outfit: str|None, hair: str|None, emotion_label: str|None, expression: FACSExpression|None, pose: PosePayload|None}
- output_dir: str
- naming_template: str, default something like '{character}_{outfit}_{emotion}_{pose}.png' with sensible fallback text (e.g. 'base'/'neutral') when a field is None -- do not let the template produce colliding filenames for distinct combos
- transparent: bool = True (sprite mode never composites over a background -- do not add a background_path field)

Implement SpriteSetSpec.expand() -> list[tuple[str, RenderRequest]] returning (output_filename, RenderRequest) pairs, one per combo, with output_path set into output_dir per the naming template.

Validate combo outfit/hair names against the registry's CharacterRecord.outfits/.hair when the registry has entries for the character (skip validation gracefully if the character has none registered yet, since Phase 2 -- outfit authoring -- may not have landed). Reference docs/posable_bones.json and docs/facs_controls.json in a docstring as the source of truth for valid pose bone names / FACS control names when constructing combos, but do not hardcode their contents into this module.

Context: this is Phase 1 of C:\Users\ghirp\.claude\plans\now-let-s-plan-for-atomic-wadler.md. Read that file for full background before starting.
acceptance_criteria:
- scarecrow_pipeline/sprite_set.py exists with SpriteSetSpec and .expand()
- expand() returns one (filename, RenderRequest) per combo, RenderRequest.model_validate() succeeds on each
- Filenames are unique across a spec with multiple combos differing only in emotion or only in outfit
- A pytest in tests/test_pipeline.py covers: basic expansion count, filename uniqueness, and that an unregistered outfit name raises/warns per the chosen validation behavior
- python -m pytest tests/ -q passes
close_reason: Added sprite_set.py with SpriteSetSpec/.expand() and 3 new pytest cases; all tests pass

title: Phase 4: Environment/set asset onboarding
description: Environments must support BOTH DAZ-sourced sets/props (via existing Diffeomorphic pipeline) AND natively Blender-importable assets from other DCCs/engines (Blender, Unreal, Unity, etc. in FBX/glTF/OBJ/USD/Alembic or whatever bpy.ops.import_scene.*/wm.*_import supports). Add blender/import_environment_asset.py: generic dispatcher -- DAZ-sourced sets via the same easy_import_daz path as import_daz_artifact.py, or the matching native Blender import operator by file extension for everything else. Both paths normalize into an Environment_<name> collection with a consistent contract (bounding box, any embedded cameras/lights tagged so render_scene() can find/use or override them). Extends the Phase 0 registry with environment records. Verification: onboard one DAZ-sourced environment/prop and one non-DAZ asset (e.g. glTF/FBX test scene) headlessly; confirm both produce correctly-named, correctly-bounded collections; feed one into Phase 3's 3d-environment render test.

title: Phase 3: Multi-character CG scene compositing
description: The one phase requiring real architecture, not additive extension. Bug to fix first: apply_pose/apply_expression in worker.py grab the FIRST armature in the scene (next(obj for obj in bpy.data.objects if obj.type=='ARMATURE')) -- correct for one character, silently wrong for N; must become explicitly per-character. Add scarecrow_pipeline/schemas.py:SceneRequest (new, additive -- RenderRequest untouched): characters: list[CharacterPlacement] (character/master_blend/outfit/hair/pose/expression + world-space placement transform) + shared camera/lighting + background: BackgroundSpec (union of image_plate mode reusing compositor.py AlphaOver extended for N characters, and 3d_environment mode with no 2D compositing, characters positioned into a pre-imported environment collection from Phase 4). Add blender/worker.py:render_scene(scene_request) alongside (not replacing) render(). Verification: two-character headless render (needs Phase 2/4 second character or environment, or two placements of Jason Cross as a stand-in) confirming no armature/property cross-talk, coherent shared lighting, both characters correctly posed independently; repeat for both backdrop modes.

title: Replace deprecated World.use_nodes usage in worker.py (removed in Blender 6.0)
description: blender/worker.py:177 sets world.use_nodes = True, which prints 'DeprecationWarning: World.use_nodes is expected to be removed in Blender 6.0' on every headless render under Blender 5.1.2. Not currently breaking (Scene.use_nodes was the same pattern and still functions), but should be replaced with whatever World API Blender 6.0 settles on before upgrading the pinned Blender version in config/toolchain.json. Noticed during scarecrow-uc0.3 verification.

title: Phase 5: Natural-language entry point - Ren'Py tag parser
description: The actual kickoff mechanism: a string describing the desired image (multi-character posing + scene), extracted from tagged comments in .rpy files. Proposed tag convention (strawman, revise freely): a comment block immediately preceding a Ren'Py image/scene statement, e.g. '# scarecrow: <description>' followed by 'image <tag> = ...'. Add scripts/extract_scene_tags.py: scans a Ren'Py project's .rpy files for this convention, emits a manifest of {renpy_tag, description, source_file, line} entries. Defines but does NOT implement the next step's contract: each extracted description is meant to be translated (by an external LLM step, out of scope) into a RenderRequest or SceneRequest, using docs/posable_bones.json + docs/facs_controls.json as the controlled vocabulary, and the registry to know which characters/environments/outfits exist. Verification: run the extractor against a small sample .rpy file with 2-3 tagged comments; confirm correct {tag, description} pairs, including multi-line descriptions and correct source-line attribution.
